title: Nine Years in Limbo: Why Rohingya Repatriation Remains Stalled
gist: Nearly nine years after Myanmar's 2017 military crackdown drove more than 750,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh, Dhaka has set up a national committee to coordinate repatriation, but the author argues the binding constraint sits inside Myanmar, not in Bangladeshi administration. The piece reframes the crisis as political, legal, security, judicial and geopolitical rather than logistical, implying large-scale return stays off the table indefinitely.

insights.claim: Myanmar's 2017 military crackdown forced more than 750,000 Rohingya to flee into Bangladesh, and Bangladesh has now hosted more than 1.2 million Rohingya for nearly a decade.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Siraj
insights.so_what: A 1.2 million-person hosting burden with no exit path is a structural fiscal and aid-dependency line item for Bangladesh and a permanent call on international humanitarian funding.
insights.quote: Nearly nine years after the 2017 military crackdown that forced more than 750,000 Rohingya to flee to Bangladesh, the prospect of their repatriation to Myanmar remains as distant as ever.
insights.locator: Nearly nine years after the 2017 military crackdown

insights.claim: The Rohingya displacement in Bangladesh is characterized as one of the world's most protracted refugee crises, now approaching its tenth year with repatriation prospects no closer than at the outset.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Siraj
insights.so_what: Protracted-crisis status means budgeting for permanent camp infrastructure and host-community friction, not transitional relief.
insights.locator: one of the world's most protracted refugee crises

insights.claim: Bangladesh recently established a national committee to strengthen coordination and develop a comprehensive strategy for the safe, voluntary and sustainable return of the Rohingya.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Siraj
insights.so_what: Signals Dhaka is building formal machinery for return, which is where donor engagement and diplomatic pressure will now be channeled.
insights.locator: Bangladesh recently took an important institutional step

insights.claim: Improved coordination inside Bangladesh cannot by itself resolve a crisis whose causes lie across the border in Myanmar, making domestic institutional reform necessary but insufficient.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Siraj
insights.so_what: Discount headlines about Bangladeshi committees or strategies as repatriation catalysts; the variable to watch is conditions inside Myanmar.
insights.quote: The committee deserves recognition, but better coordination within Bangladesh alone cannot resolve a crisis the roots of which lie across the border.

insights.claim: Rohingya repatriation should be analyzed as a political, legal, security, judicial and geopolitical problem rather than a logistical or humanitarian one, which means it requires structural change inside Myanmar plus sustained international engagement.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Siraj
insights.so_what: A framework for triaging news flow: aid pledges and camp logistics move nothing; Myanmar legal-status and security-sector change is the only real trigger.
insights.quote: Rohingya repatriation is not primarily a logistical or humanitarian challenge. It is a political, legal, security, judicial, and geopolitical problem that demands structural change inside Myanmar
insights.locator: Rohingya repatriation is not primarily a logistical

insights.claim: Large-scale Rohingya return will remain unattainable until the conditions that originally drove them from their homes in Myanmar are fundamentally addressed.
insights.speaker: Mohammed Siraj
insights.so_what: Base case is continued indefinite encampment, so plan around a multi-year status quo rather than a repatriation event.
